newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes higher on Tokyo's rise.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes higher on Tokyo's rise.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices rose at the close after a higher Tokyo market prompted some local shortcovering, dealers said.
Expectation of short supply due to wet weather in certain parts of rubber-growing areas also firmed prices, they said adding that some Far-East enquiries also underpinned sentiment.
"If Taiwan and South Korea are underbought, there is a possibility that they may come into the market," a dealer said.
"The market was firm. Sellers are reserved and waiting for higher prices on expectations of a short supply because of the wet weather," a dealer at a trading firm said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board set market indicator price for new trading month October RSS1 buyer at 332.50 cents ($1.33) a kg, while October SMR 20 buyer was up four cents at 318 cents.
Traders quoted SMR10 sellers at 318-320 cents, SMR CV at 380, SMR L at 358 and drum latex FOB at 250-252.
The INRO five-day average was 249.00 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on August 30 from 247.90 on August 29. The daily indicator was 250.94 against 250.80.
